content: A rare and often fatal cancer known as hepatosplenic T-cell lymphoma has been reported in individuals receiving this medication in combination with other drugs, such as azathioprine or 6-mercaptopurine, for the treatment of Crohn's disease or ulcerative colitis. It is essential to discuss the potential risks and benefits of this treatment with your doctor. This medication is used to treat specific types of arthritis, including rheumatoid arthritis, psoriatic arthritis, and arthritis of the spine. It is also prescribed for certain bowel diseases, such as Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis, as well as a severe skin condition called chronic plaque psoriasis. These conditions involve the immune system attacking healthy tissues in the body. Infliximab works by inhibiting the activity of a natural substance in the body called tumor necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-alpha). Before starting infliximab, read the Medication Guide provided by your pharmacist, and review it again each time you receive a refill. This medication is administered via intravenous injection over a period of at least two hours, as directed by your doctor. The dosage is determined based on your medical condition, weight, and response to treatment. Infusion reactions may occur during the administration of this drug. To minimize these side effects, your doctor may prescribe additional medications before each treatment. Notify your doctor immediately if you experience symptoms of infusion reactions, such as pain or swelling at the injection site, shortness of breath, flushing, chills, fever, or headache. If you are using this medication at home, ensure you are thoroughly trained by a healthcare professional on its preparation and administration. Do not shake the medication. Inspect the product visually for particles or discoloration before use; if either is present, do not use the liquid. To achieve the maximum benefit, use this medication regularly as prescribed. Common side effects may include headache, stomach pain, or nausea. Remember, this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Rarely, this drug may cause severe, potentially fatal liver disease. Heart problems, such as heart attacks, may occur during the infusion or within 24 hours afterward. Serious allergic reactions to this drug are rare. This is not a comprehensive list of possible side effects. In the United States, contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for similar guidance. Before using infliximab, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, other infliximab products, or any other substances. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could trigger allergic reactions or other issues. Infliximab can increase your susceptibility to infections or worsen existing infections. Avoid contact with individuals who have infections that can spread easily, such as chickenpox, COVID-19, measles, or the flu. Inform your healthcare provider that you are using infliximab before receiving any immunizations or vaccinations. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when absolutely necessary, as it may harm an unborn baby. Discuss the risks and benefits with your doctor. While this drug may pass into breast milk, it is unlikely to harm a nursing infant. Drug interactions may alter the effectiveness of your medications or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. In case of an overdose with serious symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. While using this medication, regular lab and medical tests, such as complete blood counts, liver function tests, skin exams, and Pap smears, should be conducted. Keep all medical and lab appointments. If you miss a dose, contact your doctor or pharmacist promptly to establish a new dosing schedule. For storage, consult the product instructions and your pharmacist. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Your medical condition may cause complications in emergencies. Always ensure your healthcare providers are aware of your condition. This information was last revised in May 2024. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete and personalized information about this product and your specific health needs.
